text:
Good evening,

My lease with Kirschbaum Property Ltd for the flat at Mühleweg 73 in Wädenswil, signed in January 2024, has no built-in increases. There's no schedule saying the rent goes up by a fixed amount every year, just one monthly figure, CHF 1720.

Nor is the rent tied to inflation. The contract has no clause linking it to the consumer price index or any other index. I read it through twice to be sure.

All the same, on 2 June 2026 I received a form from Ms Kate Palmer telling me my rent is going up to CHF 1865 a month from 1 October. That's CHF 145 more each month, well over CHF 1700 a year.

I attach the form so you can read it for yourself.

The reasons she gives are twofold. First, she says the landlord's financing costs have risen because the mortgage reference rate went up. Second, she says Kirschbaum replaced the old oil heating with a heat pump in May and that part of this investment is being passed on to the tenants. The heat pump is real, the workers were here for three weeks, but as far as I know the reference rate has actually gone down, not up, so I don't see how that part can be right. My neighbour Leo Egli, who has lived here much longer, is convinced the whole calculation is inflated.

Is it worth challenging this, and how would I go about it? I know there may be a deadline and I'm worried I'm already late.

Best wishes,
David Carter
